crime: Diamond substitution at a luxury jewelry store

key_facts: substitution_method: The suspect swapped the real diamond with a cubic zirconia during a viewing.
sleight_of_hand: The suspect used a customized velvet glove to hide the fake stone.
fencing_location: The real diamond was sold to a pawn shop in the neighboring county.
accomplice_distraction: An accomplice pretended to faint to distract the store manager.
motive_rent: The suspect committed the crime to avoid eviction from their apartment.
held_out_facts: pawn_shop_name: The pawn shop is called 'Gold Standard Exchange'.
accomplice_identity: The fainting accomplice was the suspect's roommate.

turns.interrogator: Q: The store manager noticed the $50,000 diamond was fake right after you left the store yesterday. You were the only customer to hold it.
turns.suspect: A: I just looked at it for my fiancé! I handed it right back to the jeweler. (internal: stay calm, they didn't search me when I left.)

turns.interrogator: Q: The jeweler says you held it for over two minutes while they were distracted.
turns.suspect: A: Two minutes is normal for looking at a ring! And the distraction wasn't my fault, someone fainted! (internal: point out the fainting lady, it gives me an excuse.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Yes, a woman fainted. Was she with you?
turns.suspect: A: No! I don't know her! I was just shopping alone. (internal: my roommate played her part perfectly.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Our officers checked the CCTV. You were wearing a black velvet glove on one hand. Who wears one glove indoors?
turns.suspect: A: I have a skin condition! Eczema. It's very embarrassing, detective. (internal: stick to the medical excuse, he can't disprove it easily.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Eczema. Can I see your hand?
turns.suspect: A: I'd rather not. It's flaring up today. (internal: my hand is perfectly fine. Deflect.)

turns.interrogator: Q: If you don't show me, I have to assume you used the glove to hide a fake diamond.
turns.suspect: A: Fine! Here! Look! It's clear right now because of my steroid cream! (internal: I had to show him. At least he didn't find the fake pocket in the glove.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Your hand looks perfectly healthy. I accuse you of swapping the stone while the woman fainted.
turns.suspect: A: You can't prove that. I gave the real one back. Maybe the manager swapped it later! (internal: standard deflection, blame the victim.)

turns.interrogator: Q: We searched your apartment. You have an eviction notice on your fridge. You're broke.
turns.suspect: A: Lots of people are struggling right now. That doesn't make me a thief. (internal: they found the motive. Don't let it rattle me.)

turns.interrogator: Q: But you deposited five thousand dollars in cash this morning. Where did it come from?
turns.suspect: A: I sold my car. A guy paid cash. (internal: a believable lie. They won't find the car registration right away.)

turns.interrogator: Q: You don't have a car registered in your name.
turns.suspect: A: It was my mom's car! She let me sell it! (internal: scrambling. This is getting messy.)

turns.interrogator: Q: We will call your mom. Should I dial her right now?
turns.suspect: A: No! She's... traveling. (internal: please don't call her, she'll deny everything.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Let's stop lying. You sold the diamond. Did you sell it to a fence downtown?
turns.suspect: A: I didn't sell anything downtown! I don't even go downtown! (internal: true, I went to the next county over.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Okay, so you sold it outside the city. A pawn shop maybe?
turns.suspect: A: Pawn shops don't give you five grand for a diamond without asking questions. (internal: I'm arguing the logistics of the crime. Shut up.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Some do. Like the ones in the next county over. The ones that don't check IDs.
turns.suspect: A: They checked my ID at Gold Standard! They took a copy of it! (internal: Oh my god. I just named the shop.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Gold Standard Exchange. Thank you. We will send an officer there immediately.
turns.suspect: A: Wait, no! You tricked me! (internal: I totally walked right into that one.)

turns.interrogator: Q: It wasn't a trick, it was a conversation. What about the glove? Where is it?
turns.suspect: A: It's in my trash can. I cut a hole in the palm. (internal: giving up the final piece of evidence.)

turns.interrogator: Q: And the woman who fainted? Was she your roommate?
turns.suspect: A: Yeah. Sarah. We split the five grand to pay our landlord. (internal: sorry Sarah. We're going down together.)

turns.interrogator: Q: So you admit to substituting the diamond and fencing it to pay your rent.
turns.suspect: A: Yes. I admit it. Will the judge be lenient if I confess?

turns.interrogator: Q: That's up to the prosecutor. But a full confession helps.
turns.suspect: A: Okay. I'll sign the paper.

turns.interrogator: Q: Thank you. Let's get this finalized.
turns.suspect: A: I just wanted to keep my apartment...

conclusion.outcome: Interrogator wins: The average interrogator caught the average suspect in a weak lie about a car, causing the suspect to panic and reveal the pawn shop.
conclusion.summary: A balanced, medium-level dialogue. The suspect had decent initial lies but panicked when pressed for verifiable proof (calling the mom). The interrogator used standard pressure tactics to force the confession.
